source.document: Ten Advances in Mathematics and Theoretical Computer Science
source.normalized_statement: For every positive dimension n, a full-dimensional compact convex body K in real n-space with barycenter zero and with zero as its only interior lattice point has ordinary Euclidean volume at most (n+1)^n/n!. The bound is attained by the translated dilation (n+1)Delta_n-(1,...,1). No classification of all equality cases is asserted.

definition_concordance.analysis: A function on Fin n is the standard coordinate model of real n-dimensional Euclidean space used by mathlib's canonical volume measure.

The name normalizedVolume is potentially misleading, but the definition is the canonical finite-dimensional Lebesgue volume converted from ENNReal to Real, with no extra factorial or lattice normalization.

definition_concordance.lean_encoding: (normalizedVolume K)^-1 • integral x in K, x dvolume
definition_concordance.analysis: This is the usual centroid formula. The theorem's compactness and nonempty-interior hypotheses ensure the finite positive-volume regime relevant to the source statement.

definition_concordance.lean_encoding: Convex Real S, IsCompact S, and (interior S).Nonempty
definition_concordance.analysis: In finite-dimensional real coordinate space, nonempty interior is the standard full-dimensional condition; the set-level theorem separately carries convexity and compactness.

definition_concordance.source_concept: only interior lattice point is zero
definition_concordance.analysis: integerPoint casts coordinatewise from Fin n -> Int and membership is taken in the topological interior, matching int(K) intersection Z^n = {0}.
The Lean expression is the source constant (n+1)^n/n! with the dimension represented as a positive natural number.

definition_concordance.lean_encoding: centeredSimplex n = simplexDilation n '' standardSimplex n
definition_concordance.analysis: simplexDilation sends x to (n+1)x-1 coordinatewise, which is precisely the source witness (n+1)Delta_n-(1,...,1).

hypothesis_concordance.analysis: The Lean theorem explicitly excludes dimension zero, matching the ordinary positive-dimensional statement and the sharpness witness theorem.
The three hypotheses decompose the source phrase into exact structural predicates without dropping boundedness, closure, convexity, or full dimensionality.

hypothesis_concordance.source_concept: centered with unique interior lattice point
hypothesis_concordance.lean_encoding: hcentered : barycenter S = 0 and hlattice : interiorLatticePoints S = {0}
hypothesis_concordance.analysis: Both source restrictions are explicit theorem hypotheses rather than hidden fields or consequences of an unrelated predicate.

conclusion_concordance.analysis: After the volume-definition correspondence, the Lean inequality has the same direction, dimension dependence, exponent, and denominator as source Theorem 1.1.

conclusion_concordance.lean_encoding: exists_centeredBody_sharp together with barycenter_centeredSimplex and normalizedVolume_centeredSimplex
conclusion_concordance.analysis: The direct existential theorem supplies a CenteredBody with exact sharp volume, while the named simplex lemmas identify the advertised witness and its barycenter and volume.

nonvacuity.reason: The Comparator-checked existential theorem constructs a CenteredBody for every positive n and asserts exact equality with the sharp constant. Thus the theorem domain is inhabited and the bound is not vacuously true through an empty body class.

scope_exclusions: No uniqueness or classification of all equality cases is certified; the source explicitly leaves that refinement open.
This audit does not independently replay the internal analytic proof beyond the already-clear kernel and Comparator gates.

disposition.reason: The source theorem, all load-bearing definitions, hypotheses, inequality, and sharpness witness have direct or equivalent Lean encodings, and a checked explicit witness clears nonvacuity. The only excluded source discussion is the unproved classification of all equality cases, which the Lean targets do not claim.
